diffs.diff: header pin 4: part says SDA, datasheet reading says NC
diffs.evidence: Infineon's official 'DPS3xx Pressure Shield2Go' pinout graphic gives physical pin 4 = I2C: SDA. Its physical numbering is 1 NC, 2 NC, 3 NC, 4 I2C: SDA, 5 I2C: SCL, 6 Ground, 7 Power 3.3V, 8 INT/GPIO3, 9 NC on the 9-pin header, then 10 NC, 11 NC, 12 NC, 13 NC, 14 SPI: CS, 15 SPI: SCLK, 16 SPI: MOSI, 17 SPI: MISO on the 8-pin header. The part uses this order exactly. The second reading has the same two headers and signals, but it lists the 8-pin SPI header first and the 9-pin header second, so its pin positions are shifted. This is an ordering difference, not different wiring. Infineon's board photo (dps368-shield2go.png) confirms the silkscreen rows: NC NC NC SDA SCL GND 3V3 INT/GPIO3 NC and NC NC NC NC CS SCLK MOSI MISO.

diffs.diff: pressure_Pa: datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has -0.0004921, -0.002205, 1000, 1000
diffs.evidence: The DPS368 has no fixed per-count conversion. Datasheet sec. 4.9.1/4.9.2: 'Traw_sc = Traw/kT', 'Praw_sc = Praw/kP', 'Tcomp (°C) = c0*0.5 + c1*Traw_sc', 'Pcomp(Pa) = c00 + Praw_sc*(c10 + Praw_sc*(c20 + Praw_sc*c30)) + Traw_sc*c01 + Traw_sc*Praw_sc*(c11 + Praw_sc*c21)'. Here c0..c30 are per-chip factory coefficients (regs 0x10-0x21) and kP/kT come from table 9. The second reading's '1 per count' only says that the compensated outputs are in Pa and °C. The driver implements these formulas exactly. The sim's scales come from the same formulas applied to its own coefficient registers: c0=204, c1=-258, so T = 102 + (-258/524288)*Traw = -0.0004921 °C per count with offset 102. c00=98500 Pa, c10=-56000, kP=253952 (16x), so P = 985 hPa + (-56000/253952/100) = -0.002205 hPa per count. The 1000 scales only encode the MEAS_CFG ready-flag register, not a conversion. The simulator test passes (T=23.70C P=962.45hPa).
